scope: Native Linux x86-64 Java/native allocation-message integration through the actual Maven-built tooling JAR; not the complete scheduler

inputs.jar_recovery: The identical JAR is embedded in docs/evidence/java-allocation-messages.json; native classes were not substituted

acceptance.actual_native_denials: two concurrent native threads; a denied retry receives a fresh wait identity
acceptance.production_codec: ready, blocked and granted events decoded by AllocationMessages from actual JAR; permissions generated by that codec and consumed by injected hook
acceptance.permission_results: accepted, duplicate and unknown retained distinctly; stale grants do not release fresh or peer waits
acceptance.fixture_controls: query, park and allowance diagnostics use a separate listener and are never accepted by the production decoder
acceptance.native_rejections: eleven malformed/range/identity/version/field controls each report script error and leave both actual condition waits unchanged before owner cancellation
acceptance.cancellation: Two native condition waiters terminate with actual root exit status 137.
acceptance.normal_completion: Root exits 0; memory endpoints and errno 0 are verified; original limits are restored; twelve later matching allocations succeed through reused slots.
acceptance.numeric_selection: Frida UInt64 paired-input probe establishes alternate-spelling acceptance and overflow saturation; round-trip equality plus positive signed-long bound preserve required wait distinctions
acceptance.cleanup: All 30 target/supervisor PIDs are absent; cgroup and scratch are removed; SSH exits 0 and all hosted cleanup posts pass; the workflow retains deliberate exit 17.

limits: Controlled 256 MiB malloc fixture, not general allocator/descendant coverage or physical-memory pressure
Native queue/batching/JobQueue adapter and actual Cargo/Bazel scheduling remain unaccepted
Other-platform maintained-runtime protocol integration remains required
Native malformed-control checks have eleven explicit cases; they do not establish exhaustive protocol input coverage
Existing native-producer linker/JVM stack-permission warnings remain visible
